clue.text: Force legal action to be taken about a scoundrel

indicators.note: taken about tells you the lawsuit word goes round the outside of the rogue

parts.note: a case is a legal action brought in court
a cad is an old-fashioned word for a scoundrel

explanation.surface: Someone urges that a rogue be taken to court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Force' looks like a verb meaning compel, but it is a noun: in northern England a force is a waterfall, as in High Force in Teesdale.
explanation.definitionFit: Northern English dialect noun for a waterfall, which is what this torrent of tumbling water is.

clue.text: Competitor not in favour of a certain proposal

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
a tender is a formal offer to do work at a stated price, one kind of proposal

explanation.surface: A rival opposes a particular motion.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone taking part in a contest with a chance of winning is a rival.

clue.text: Check on a boy's upbringing — it's a disgrace

parts.note: to scan something is to check it over

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing a word up means writing it from the bottom to the top

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: Someone looks into how a boy was raised and finds it shameful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upbringing' is not about childhood: in a down entry it sends LAD upwards, giving DAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an outrage that brings public shame.

clue.text: The new senator is to make a statement

indicators.note: new says the letters of the following two words are given a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A freshly elected senator is about to address the public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges SENATOR IS; it does not describe the politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a declaration made firmly as fact.

clue.text: Note a high-minded individual's bearing

parts.note: E is a note of the musical scale
a saint, abbreviated ST, is a person of lofty virtue

explanation.surface: Observe how a principled person carries themself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bearing' reads as posture or manner, but it is a compass direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: one of the compass directions a navigator may take.

clue.text: Cover an article in tin or lead

parts.note: to cap something is to cover its top

indicators.note: in places the article inside the metal word

parts.note: taken as written
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Wrap an item in one of two metals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' looks like the metal beside tin, but it is the verb to command.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a verb: to skipper a team is to command it.

clue.text: Close man — he represented fickle people

indicators.note: read as re-presented, it says the letters before it are presented again in another order

explanation.surface: A secretive man acted on behalf of unreliable folk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represented' is re-presented: the letters of CLOSE MAN HE are set out afresh.
explanation.definitionFit: Figurative sense: like the colour-changing lizards, such folk shift their views to suit the company.

clue.text: Quietly consume about fifty and double up!

indicators.note: about puts the first two pieces round the Roman numeral

parts.note: P, for piano, is the musical marking for quietly
to eat is to consume
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Someone silently scoffs some fifty items and is bent over with stomach ache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'double up' suggests bending in pain; here it means folding cloth back on itself.
explanation.definitionFit: To fold fabric back over itself, which doubles its thickness.

clue.text: Inoffensive, lacking aspiration, so short of members

indicators.note: lacking says the breathy letter is missing from the word for inoffensive

parts.note: harmless means inoffensive
aspiration is the breathy sound of the letter H

explanation.surface: A club too bland and unambitious has trouble recruiting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aspiration' is not ambition but the sounded H, and 'members' are limbs, not people who join.
explanation.definitionFit: Punning description: limbs are bodily members, and two of them are missing here.

clue.text: Dope obtainable from a hostelry in New York

indicators.note: in places the pub inside the city's abbreviation

parts.note: an inn is a hostelry

explanation.surface: Drugs can be bought at a Manhattan bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' reads as drugs, but it means a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym in the slang sense of a foolish person.

clue.text: Poles carrying listening equipment make approaches

indicators.note: carrying says the two poles hold the hearing organ between them

parts.note: N and S are the north and south poles
the ear is the body's equipment for listening

explanation.surface: Polish agents with bugging gear make contact with someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' are not people from Poland but north and south.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: draws close to something.

clue.text: Politicians ordering means test

indicators.note: ordering says the letters of the two following words are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Members of the government demand that benefits depend on income.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordering' rearranges MEANS TEST rather than meaning commanding.
explanation.definitionFit: Respected senior figures in government are one kind of these.

clue.text: Close by a river or brook

parts.note: the close of something is its end
the Ure is a river in North Yorkshire, England

explanation.surface: A spot near a river or a small stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brook' looks like a stream beside the river, but it is the verb to tolerate.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: to tolerate or put up with something.

clue.text: The relay can be tough

indicators.note: can be says the letters before it are able to become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A team running race is hard going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be' rearranges THE RELAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes meat or skin that is hard and resistant, like hide.

clue.text: Stopping the ball — grabbing two points first

indicators.note: grabbing says the word for a ball takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance
E and S, east and south, are two points of the compass
1st, written IST, is first

explanation.surface: A goalkeeper saves a shot after seizing two points earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ball' is a formal dance, not something kicked, and 'first' is 1st with the numeral read as I.
explanation.definitionFit: A rare noun for the act of ceasing or leaving off.

clue.text: A little model Hindus make in India

indicators.note: A little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A handful of exemplary Hindus manufacture goods in India.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the whole clue points to a city that a small part of India's Hindus make up.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital territory is a place located in that country, which the clue's closing words allude to.

clue.text: Worked out cut without hesitation

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside puts the word for cut round the hesitation

parts.note: excised means cut out
er is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: Someone calculated a reduction straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' carries its old sense of outside, so it signals a container rather than a removal; 'Worked out' is gym training, not calculating.
explanation.definitionFit: Trained the body physically, as in a gym session.

clue.text: "The ____ shows the man, as morning shows the day" (Milton)

definitions.text: "The ____ shows the man, as morning shows the day" (Milton)

parts.words: "The ____ shows the man, as morning shows the day" (Milton)
parts.note: a line from Milton's Paradise Regained with one word left blank for the solver to supply

explanation.surface: A line of Milton with a word missing.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word of the quotation: a person's early years foretell the adult, as dawn foretells the day.

clue.text: Courtesy causing hold up in French church

parts.note: to defer something is to hold it up or delay it
en is the French word for in
CE is the abbreviation for the Church of England

explanation.surface: Politeness delays a robbery in a French church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hold up' is a delay, not a robbery.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: polite respect shown to another's wishes.

clue.text: Note the temporary accommodation — one has to take on the maintenance

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
a tent is somewhere to stay for a short time
I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A warning that whoever takes the short-term lodgings must also pay for upkeep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' looks like an instruction to observe, but it is the sol-fa note RE.
explanation.definitionFit: The act of keeping or holding on to something, such as staff or heat.

clue.text: Occupies a number of workers

parts.note: ten is a number
worker ants are a standard crossword sense of workers

explanation.surface: Something keeps several employees busy.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb: lives in a property as a paying occupant.

clue.text: A player's shot if including no loud music!

indicators.note: including says the word if takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
F, for forte, is the musical marking for loud

explanation.surface: A musician would have a go provided nothing noisy is played.
explanation.walkthrough: 'player' is not a musician: in billiards and snooker this is a shot where the cue ball goes into a pocket off another ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A billiards stroke in which the cue ball is pocketed after striking another ball.

clue.text: The figure of a military officer wearing a tab

parts.note: OC is the abbreviation for Officer Commanding
someone wearing a tab has a tag on

explanation.surface: The shape of an army officer with a staff badge on his collar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'figure' is a geometric shape, not the officer's physique.
explanation.definitionFit: A geometric shape with eight sides.

clue.text: Family quarrel coming to an end?

definitions.text: Family quarrel coming to an end?

parts.words: Family quarrel coming to an end?
parts.note: a blood feud between families is one that tends to finish only when lives are ended

explanation.surface: A domestic row is finally settled.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a row being patched up; the grim reading is a feud whose aim is someone's death.
explanation.definitionFit: A blood feud between clans, pursued until somebody is killed.

clue.text: It's incumbent to have transport after six

indicators.note: after tells you the vehicle follows the numeral in the answer

parts.note: VI is the Roman numeral for six
a car is a means of transport

explanation.surface: It is necessary to arrange a lift for the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incumbent' reads as obligatory, but as a noun it is the holder of a church living.
explanation.definitionFit: The holder of a Church of England parish post is called by this noun.

clue.text: Late turn? Right!

parts.note: ex means former, as late does of someone no longer in a post
a turn is an act in a variety show

explanation.surface: A driver nearly misses a junction and is told which way to go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' is a stage performance and 'Right' means correct, not a direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: precisely correct.

clue.text: A newspaper leader

parts.note: a leader is usually a paper's opinion article, but here it means the person who leads the paper

explanation.definitionFit: The person in charge of a paper's content, rather than its opinion column.

clue.text: Publicise a set-up in song

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the letters are written from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to air a view is to make it public

explanation.surface: A singer exposes a sting through a lyric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set-up' sends AIR plus A upwards; it is not a trap.
explanation.definitionFit: A solo vocal piece in an opera.

clue.text: It holds for certain — no wobbling

indicators.note: wobbling says the letters of the nearby words are unsteady and move about

explanation.surface: A shelf bracket stays firm without any shaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wobbling' rearranges CERTAIN and NO.
explanation.definitionFit: A box, jar or similar vessel that has things kept inside it.

clue.text: An instrument or mount turned over

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: turned over says the word for a horse is written back to front

parts.note: a nag is a horse, which a rider mounts

explanation.surface: A tool or its stand has been flipped upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mount' is a horse, NAG, which 'turned over' makes GAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A keyboard instrument with pipes, found in churches.

clue.text: Put into the regular procedure as a favour

indicators.note: into says the first word goes inside the word for routine

parts.note: rote is fixed mechanical routine
to set something down is to put it there

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a job to be slotted into the usual routine as a kindness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'favour' is not a kindness but a ribbon badge worn to show support.
explanation.definitionFit: A ribbon badge worn by a supporter, the old sense of the word.

clue.text: Quite slow — notedly so

parts.note: notedly hints at musical notes: a tempo marking for a moderately slow, walking pace

explanation.surface: Someone is famously sluggish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notedly' pretends to mean famously; it points to written music.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian tempo direction telling musicians to play at a walking pace.
